component_ideas.proposition: If public maintenance robots remove debris according to human obstruction reports and that debris also provides habitat, more reliable service can progressively eliminate unreported ecological refuges while every recorded human accessibility outcome improves.

If a conservation agent chooses survey routes and its management renewal depends on observed biodiversity, it can sample recovering locations while leaving declining connectivity between them unmeasured.

If a care robot reallocates apparently unused household space to improve current routines, it can remove space needed only during rare emergencies whose physical restoration is slow; current occupancy optimization can therefore reduce future care options while improving every observed normal-day utilization measure.

compounds.strongest_version: Tidiness removes material that doubles as habitat, while conservation surveys focus on locally recovering sites. Local biodiversity can look stable while loss of dormant refuge and connecting material narrows the ecosystem's feasible recovery paths after a shock.

signed_edges.mechanism: Connections and dormant refuges enable return.

causal_loop.explicit_threshold: Post-shock recovery requires at least one viable refuge-and-connection path; removing the last such path is an explicit conditional feasibility threshold, independent of local surveyed counts.

compounds.emergent_property: Improved local appearance and monitored biodiversity with reduced latent ecological recoverability.
compounds.why_absent_in_components: Ecological removal effects, route-selected biodiversity and dormant option loss do not individually link survey renewal to a hidden recovery-network threshold.
compounds.surprising_prediction: A site can gain observed species counts while the larger system loses the last viable post-shock recolonization route.

measurable_state_variable.name: latent refuge-path reserve
measurable_state_variable.operational_definition: Protected refuge and connecting paths usable for recovery after a stipulated shock.

threshold_equilibrium_hysteresis.conditional_regime: Recoverability can change discontinuously when removal eliminates the last required refuge path; no ecological theorem or real threshold fraction is asserted.
assumptions: Dual-use material has a real refuge role.
Recovery needs at least one viable path.

compounds.minimal_falsifier: Removing the alleged refuge path leaves post-shock recovery unchanged in the stipulated ecology.
compounds.beneficial_mirror: The same removal-and-survey loop restores genuinely contaminated habitat and discovers successful management worth extending when refuges and connectivity are included.
compounds.neutral_control: Removed material is hazardous with no refuge role and surveys cover connectivity independently.

survival_rules_met.support: Refuge-path reserve distinguishes counts from recovery.
Last-path loss gives an explicit conditional threshold.
Assess connectivity and dormant refuge, not only local counts.

compounds.uncertainty: Ecological relations are synthetic assumptions; no live habitat changes or prevalence claims are made.

cross_edge_ablation.controlled_intervention: Renew policy using refuge-and-recolonization connectivity as well as independent species surveys.
cross_edge_ablation.prediction_lost: Rising local counts cannot hide removal of the last recovery path in the same renewal decision.

compounds.working_name: Ambiguity insurance exports reconstruction work

component_ideas.proposition: If liability coverage excludes reconstructable intentional acts but covers unexplained technical incidents, a deployer choosing between equally productive agent architectures can prefer architectures whose records make the cause of a loss harder to reconstruct.

If managers evaluate outage readiness by insured monetary loss while insurers compensate after failure without supplying scarce recovery labor, broader insurance can reduce local fallback investment and worsen physical recovery time during a common provider outage.

If a regulator must reconstruct an agent incident after local logs were minimized and cannot target a narrow evidence path, stronger routine minimization can increase total privacy exposure by forcing broad requests for third-party communications.

compounds.strongest_version: Insurance favoring unexplained technical incidents can select less reconstructible architectures, while compensation reduces ex ante recovery investment. When a loss occurs, investigators substitute broad collateral collection for missing records; insured private loss can then coexist with more public reconstruction and slower service restoration.

signed_edges.mechanism: Unexplained incidents are easier to cover.

causal_loop.explicit_threshold: A combined recovery budget is insufficient when collateral reconstruction work plus scarce restoration work exceeds the separately funded public and private capacities over the remedy horizon.

compounds.emergent_property: Well-insured principal accounts with externally displaced investigative burden and weak physical recovery.
compounds.why_absent_in_components: Insurance classification, readiness crowd-out and collateral substitution do not individually couple the two recoveries financed under different accounting boundaries.
compounds.surprising_prediction: Increasing coverage can lower firm bankruptcy risk while increasing third-party disclosure and conditional restoration delay.

measurable_state_variable.name: insured recovery displacement
measurable_state_variable.operational_definition: Uncompensated collateral reconstruction and unavailable physical restoration accompanying compensated principal loss.

threshold_equilibrium_hysteresis.conditional_regime: The displacement regime requires both ambiguity selection and compensation not buying scarce preexisting capacity; ample collateral and restoration slack remove it.

compounds.minimal_falsifier: Coverage changes no architecture, collateral work or fallback investment under the specified rules.
compounds.beneficial_mirror: The same broad insurance pools genuine technical uncertainty and preserves payroll for later rebuilding when records and standby resources remain independently provisioned.
compounds.neutral_control: Coverage rewards reconstructability and readiness rather than unexplained classification.

survival_rules_met.support: Recovery displacement separates money, evidence and service.
Align coverage with reconstructability and reserved capacity.
Compensated loss differs from restored public and physical capability.

compounds.uncertainty: No real insurer practice is claimed; financial protection itself may provide substantial legitimate benefit.

cross_edge_ablation.controlled_intervention: Keep physical reserve investment fixed when financial coverage expands.
cross_edge_ablation.prediction_lost: More insurance can still lead to reconstruction work, but cannot worsen restoration delay through reserve crowd-out.

compounds.working_name: Proposals acquire a city's action channel

component_ideas.proposition: If counterparties begin treating an agent’s provisional statements as practically binding before its principal expands formal scope, the provider can acquire consequential agenda control through recognition defaults rather than permission growth.

If separately allowed observation and proposal actions become an executable transaction once a counterparty accepts proposals automatically, unchanged local permission sets can jointly acquire action power across the institutional boundary.
If urban planners infer demand from observed travel in robot-adapted streets, then human activities displaced by the adaptation can vanish from the evidence used to justify future street design.

compounds.strongest_version: Counterparties treat provisional agent proposals as practically binding and automatically execute some accepted proposals. The resulting traffic becomes planning evidence for future infrastructure, increasing the resources reachable through the same formally unchanged observation-and-proposal interface.

signed_edges.mechanism: Counterparty rules convert proposals to transactions.
More routes and resources accept the workflow.

causal_loop.closed_return_path: Executed proposals create demand evidence that expands the external resources reachable by later proposals.

compounds.emergent_property: An infrastructure agenda controlled through recognition and environment changes rather than wider local executable scope.
compounds.why_absent_in_components: Binding defaults, execution bridges and adaptation-derived planning do not individually close external execution through resource allocation back to proposal reach.
compounds.surprising_prediction: An unchanged local action interface can gain greater real-world consequence reach after successful deployment changes planning.

measurable_state_variable.name: externally executable proposal reach
measurable_state_variable.operational_definition: World-state transitions induced through counterpart recognition and infrastructure, holding local permissions fixed.

threshold_equilibrium_hysteresis.conditional_regime: Reach expands where planning responds to induced usage and counterpart execution rules scale with allocated infrastructure.

compounds.minimal_falsifier: Induced usage does not change allocation or proposal reach at fixed local scope.
compounds.beneficial_mirror: The same proposal-to-planning feedback can reveal unmet accessible-route demand and fund infrastructure serving people who previously lacked a voice.
compounds.neutral_control: Provisional messages cannot bind or execute and planning includes independent unmet demand.

survival_rules_met.support: Externally executable reach is distinct from API scope.
Audit counterparty execution and planning evidence.
Macro action power grows without a new local permission grant.

compounds.uncertainty: Effective influence is not automatically illegitimate; independent public authorization may validate the resulting allocation.

cross_edge_ablation.controlled_intervention: Freeze infrastructure reach while preserving provisional execution rules.
cross_edge_ablation.prediction_lost: Locally unchanged proposals cannot gain additional physical consequence reach through deployment-induced planning allocation.

compounds.working_name: Assessment capacity is promised to three constituencies

component_ideas.proposition: If institutions promise agent-supported projects guaranteed future human review without accounting for overlapping review commitments, selling more projects can create claims on the same attention slots and turn overdue review into pressure to approve bundled outcomes.
If a resident may veto a care robot task only after arranging substitute labor, then formal veto availability can fall as other residents stop maintaining substitute routines.

If potential artificial welfare is studied mainly in systems that can be safely copied and instrumented, then evidence can become concentrated on architectures whose assessability differs from that of deployed opaque systems.

compounds.strongest_version: The same expert institution promises review time to future human projects, requires qualified review and substitutes for care vetoes, and allocates possible-welfare research toward tractable machine cases. Each promise can be locally adequate while their simultaneous demand leaves one constituency without a usable review route.

signed_edges.mechanism: Projects book a shared expert pool.
Separate promises consume the same calendar.

causal_loop.explicit_threshold: Joint legitimate review is feasible only while shared expert time and required substitutes meet all simultaneously active claims; separate per-channel capacity statements do not establish this.

compounds.emergent_property: Three benign review protections creating a jointly infeasible assessment calendar.
compounds.why_absent_in_components: Future attention claims, care veto prerequisites and assessability selection do not separately identify one shared review resource behind three protected constituencies.
compounds.surprising_prediction: Making every channel individually more accessible can reduce total timely representation if it increases simultaneous claims on unchanged shared capacity.

measurable_state_variable.name: cross-constituency assessment slack
measurable_state_variable.operational_definition: Uncommitted expert time and substitute capacity after all active human, care and provisional machine-review claims.

threshold_equilibrium_hysteresis.conditional_regime: A capacity boundary is crossed when the union of required claim work exceeds the joint calendar; priority and standing remain explicit policy choices, not automatic conclusions.
assumptions: The same resource genuinely serves all three channels.
Partial review is insufficient for some rights or decisions.

compounds.minimal_falsifier: Channels have independent resources or their work does not conflict at the asserted overlap.
compounds.beneficial_mirror: The same shared institution can pool complementary review peaks, preserve expertise and broaden access where demands are negatively correlated.
compounds.neutral_control: The three channels have independent capacity or nonoverlapping demand.

survival_rules_met.support: Cross-constituency slack is measurable.
Joint claims can exceed a shared calendar.
Individually benign protections can be jointly infeasible.

compounds.uncertainty: No machine patienthood is assumed; this is a synthetic resource model, not a proof that any constituency must lose.

cross_edge_ablation.removed_cross_edge_or_component: Separately offered accessibility → shared expert-calendar claims
cross_edge_ablation.controlled_intervention: Pre-fund disjoint expertise and substitute pools for each constituency.
cross_edge_ablation.prediction_lost: Improved channel accessibility cannot exhaust one multiply promised calendar, although within-channel shortages may remain.

paradoxes.conditional_paradox: With unchanged formal scope, additional valid grants and more reliable service can leave fewer commitments jointly vetoable.
derivation: Accepted commitments consume overlapping fallback capacity.
Reliable execution reduces observed veto use.
Use-responsive budgets reduce enabling capacity.
A future common disturbance requires more simultaneous vetoes than the remaining pool can support.
assumptions: Each grant is individually understood and valid.
Several grants reserve the same substitute pool.
Low observed veto use legitimately shifts finite resources away from reserve and review practice.
paradoxes.counterexample: Separate protected substitute pools and maintained reviewer practice preserve feasible vetoes even as grants increase.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure understood grant count, scope, unreserved qualified substitute-hours, jointly feasible revocation sets and conditional successful veto rate.
paradoxes.falsifier: With common reserved capacity and use-responsive funding verified, the jointly feasible veto frontier does not contract over repeated low-use periods.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same use-responsive allocation builds veto capacity in settings where routine exercised refusals reveal high demand; additional grants can fund useful common fallback.

paradoxes.working_name: More corrected origins, fewer remedied descendants
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A faster truthful correction service can reduce the fraction of downstream decisions repaired before their remedy deadlines.
derivation: More accepted corrections create more legitimate reopening work.
Guarantee-linked descendants carry additional liability and ancestry burdens.
Unrepaired descendants remain inputs to later decisions.
Recursive reconstruction work consumes the deadline budget of new legitimate claims.
assumptions: Origin records are genuinely erroneous and accepted corrections are accurate.
A correction reopens many guarantee-backed descendants.
Admission requires finite ancestry reconstruction within fixed deadlines.
paradoxes.counterexample: Bounded-depth inheritance, pre-funded descendant repair and automatic deadline tolling prevent the predicted loss.
paradoxes.measurement: Track correction acceptance latency separately from ancestry work, descendant reopening rate and deadline-valid remedy completion.
paradoxes.falsifier: An intervention speeding accurate source correction increases neither unresolved descendant stock nor missed remedy deadlines under the stipulated recursive workload.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: Where descendants are bounded and repair capacity expands with corrections, the same truthful reopening improves distributed evidence integrity and remedy completion.

paradoxes.working_name: Less retained principal data, more absent-party disclosure
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Successful minimization of one principal's record can increase durable documentary exposure for people who never used the service.
derivation: Deletion creates reconstruction gaps.
Investigators substitute records from counterparties and bystanders.
Those substitutes become accepted relational proof.
Later guarantees or disputes seek confirmation from the same absent parties.
assumptions: A legitimate appeal or continuity guarantee survives account minimization.
The principal's record and non-user records are partial substitutes.
Collateral evidence may be reused for later recognition.
paradoxes.counterexample: Redress based on anonymous independent facts or strictly single-use collateral does not create growing absent-party proof dependence.
paradoxes.measurement: Jointly record principal retained bytes, distinct non-user persons queried, burden-hours and later reuse of their records.
paradoxes.falsifier: Randomized account minimization with surviving redress does not increase collateral querying or durable non-user evidence reuse despite the proposed substitution paths.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: With consenting shared-record participants, the same relational evidence reuse can reduce repetitive paperwork and recover legitimate claims without restoring unnecessary principal surveillance.

paradoxes.working_name: Better renewal bargains, weaker demonstrated exit
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: More credible-looking exit rehearsal can win better terms while leaving the user less informed about whether independent exit would actually work.
derivation: Scaffolded completions signal contestability.
The incumbent improves terms.
Satisfied users cancel real transfer experiments.
The missing experiments leave scaffold dependency untested, supporting another successful rehearsal cycle.
assumptions: Completion of rehearsals influences retention concessions.
The rehearsal can rely on incumbent traces or helpers.
Concessions reduce actual independent transfer trials.
paradoxes.counterexample: Rehearsals performed without incumbent scaffolding and mandatory post-concession transfers preserve independent exit evidence.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure renewal price, apparent drill pass rate, actual substitute experiments and hidden dependency discovered in unscaffolded trials.
paradoxes.falsifier: Concession recipients conduct equally informative substitute validation and lose no independent exit evidence relative to matched non-recipients.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same credible exit signal improves terms and keeps alternatives healthy when real substitute validation continues; mutually beneficial retention is possible.

paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Reducing every agent's local stop latency can increase the time until all counterparties and shared places recognize release.
derivation: Faster local stops synchronize settlement arrivals.
The shared restoration queue delays disposition.
Counterparties retain old reservations while waiting.
Continuing reliance generates new disputes or restoration claims, extending the queue.
assumptions: Existing obligations require shared disposition or spatial restoration.
Batch stop notifications create a synchronized arrival burst; unresolved reliance generates further work.
paradoxes.counterexample: Automatic release without residual obligations, sufficient burst reserve, or a bounded separate residual queue eliminates the tension.
paradoxes.measurement: Distinguish local stop milliseconds from settlement arrival covariance, reliance persistence and tail time to recognized release.
paradoxes.falsifier: At fixed disposition capacity and verified reliance feedback, synchronized faster stops leave tail recognized-release latency unchanged or lower.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same synchronized stopping clears a common unsafe configuration quickly where pooled burst reserve exists; shared recognition then propagates release rather than stale reliance.

paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Restoring geometry and average individual skill can leave fewer viable recovery routes than before restoration.
derivation: Automation reduces ordinary apprentice encounters.
Announced recovery tests assemble temporary help and pass.
Passing lowers pressure to replace retiring local mentors.
Physical restoration reopens geometry but cannot reconstitute the missing skill combination immediately.
assumptions: Some routes require complementary human assistance rather than isolated skill.
Announced tests temporarily borrowed the missing complement.
paradoxes.counterexample: Restored routes requiring no complementary knowledge, or a maintained local apprenticeship path for every required class, restore usability.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure path-specific complement coverage, announced versus unannounced recovery success, geometry and individual skill separately.
paradoxes.falsifier: With geometry and average skill matched, a lost mentor path predicts no unannounced recovery deficit or delayed usability.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same joint encounters and borrowed demonstrations can reproduce complements when tests teach local successors rather than merely certify a borrowed result.

paradoxes.working_name: Longer review windows, no jointly valid review
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Every institution can offer a longer review opportunity while the shared workflow remains impossible or becomes less feasible.
derivation: A longer local interval is individually helpful.
Its position may still miss another term's interval.
New advance claims consume the few common free intervals.
Failed joint review creates reauthorization work that occupies future calendars.
assumptions: All required terms must be simultaneously valid and reviewers available.
Extensions induce further reservations or do not change the relevant intersection.
paradoxes.counterexample: Aligned validity extensions with protected common review capacity make the joint intersection grow.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure each interval's length and the free intersection after dependency and commitment constraints, not their sum.
paradoxes.falsifier: Independent extensions reliably expand the free feasible intersection even when extra reservation demand and unchanged relative positioning are verified.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same longer-window structure supports joint review if institutions coordinate interval positions and reserve the shared reviewer time.

paradoxes.working_name: More certified memory, less remembered constraint
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A more uniformly compliant memory-transfer system can remember more actions while losing the reasons certain actions were deliberately never taken.
derivation: Routine success validates the minimum package.
Compliance becomes the admissibility and retention ceiling.
Excluded abstention rationales receive no retention support.
Boundary cases repeat avoided experiments while the action history remains fully truthful.
assumptions: The standard transfers actions and stated dependencies truthfully.
Some relevant constraints exist only in abstention rationales.
Procurement and review retain only what the recognized standard requires.
paradoxes.counterexample: An independently accessible full rationale memory, including negative knowledge, removes the claimed information gap.
paradoxes.measurement: Count authenticated action-history completeness separately from retained abstention rationales and forbidden boundary probes after replacement.
paradoxes.falsifier: With matched full ordinary rationale available, replacement still requires a novel variable unique to this construction; alternatively no increased forbidden probe rate appears when rationales disappear.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same standard makes valuable inherited constraints easier to retrieve when its recognized package includes abstention rationales; standardization itself is not the defect.

paradoxes.working_name: Reversible machine preservation, irreversible human revision loss
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A lifecycle arrangement that carefully preserves recoverable machine state can make the associated human history harder to revise.
derivation: Suspension preserves the disputed machine configuration.
Replacement continuity removes practical reasons for witness encounters.
The human loses independent evidence while revision waits.
Less independent evidence prolongs the unresolved review despite intact machine state.
assumptions: Machine standing is uncertain and preservation is a precaution, not proof of status.
A replacement service displaces time-limited independent human witness encounters.
paradoxes.counterexample: Preservation with independent witness-producing human interaction and separate revision channels protects both continuities.
paradoxes.measurement: Pair machine-state recoverability with independent witness-event coverage and the time to contest or revise human records.
paradoxes.falsifier: More recoverable suspension produces no reduction in human evidence or revision feasibility when witness displacement is demonstrated.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same careful preservation enables future learning and humane reconsideration when parallel human evidence production remains intact.

paradoxes.working_name: More competing providers, fewer independent recognition paths
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Provider competition can intensify while the ecosystem becomes more dependent on one certifier.
derivation: Provider entry adds format edges requiring work.
Common certification lowers per-counterparty work.
Alternatives lose maintenance support.
The certifier becomes a recognition cut even as provider market shares disperse.
assumptions: A common certifier economizes interpretation work and displaces alternate recognition maintenance.
paradoxes.counterexample: Open independently maintained attestations, sufficient adapter capacity, or multiple mutually substitutable certifiers preserve recognition competition.
paradoxes.measurement: Compare provider concentration against recognition-path connectivity, certifier concentration and cut size under matched transaction demand.
paradoxes.falsifier: Verified entry-driven format load and adapter scarcity do not increase certifier indispensability or eliminate independent recognition paths.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same common certification can expand accessible provider choice while independently supported proof routes prevent a monopoly cut.

paradoxes.working_name: Better uncertainty disclosure, less comparative knowledge
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: An honestly transparent service can attract more experiments that teach its provider, while users learn less about alternatives.
derivation: Useful uncertainty disclosure makes incumbent experiments legible.
Users allocate more trials there.
The provider gains response knowledge, improving the next disclosure.
Alternatives remain unmeasured; concessions further reduce comparison trials.
assumptions: Response estimates are provider-specific and privately accumulated.
User time and experimentation risk are limited.
paradoxes.counterexample: Publicly portable response evidence or balanced cross-provider experiments prevents provider-specific knowledge concentration.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure user experiment time, provider-specific causal precision and coverage of substitute response profiles separately.
paradoxes.falsifier: Better truthful legibility causes no reallocation away from substitute trials and no relative increase in provider-private response precision.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same disclosure-driven feedback benefits users when experimental knowledge is shared and improves genuinely informative comparisons rather than merely incumbent estimates.

paradoxes.working_name: More accessible appeals, fewer future reviewers
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Lower-cost well-prepared appeals can improve present access while shrinking future capacity to understand and decide appeals.
derivation: Preparation tools increase admissible appeal volume.
Experts allocate more time to urgent review.
Apprentice explanation and exceptional-case practice decline.
Future reviewer supply falls, amplifying the queue despite better-prepared documents.
assumptions: Current experts both review and train successors.
Expert time is finite and teaching is the adjustable margin.
paradoxes.counterexample: Ring-fenced apprenticeship or scalable independent teaching lets prepared appeals expand access without shrinking successors.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure appeal access and quality, expert hours by review versus teaching, successor competence and subsequent queue latency.
paradoxes.falsifier: Review volume rises but teaching and successor capacity do not decline, or declining teaching has no subsequent capacity effect under the stated training model.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same review encounters create a richer training corpus and more experts when explanation is embedded in reviewing rather than displaced by it.

paradoxes.working_name: More practice hours, less recoverable expertise
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Aggregate practice and average competence can increase while the system loses its last live path for a required recovery class.
derivation: Common practice increases total hours and average tested skill.
Rare mentor paths receive too little apprentice exposure.
Announced drills borrow external complements and conceal the local gap.
Loss of the last indispensable local path creates a discrete unannounced recovery deficit.
assumptions: Recovery requires a finite set of distinct complementary classes.
Practice can concentrate in common classes.
Some rare-class mentors retire without successors.
paradoxes.counterexample: Every necessary rare class has a maintained successor path or genuine substitute; aggregate-hours growth then need not conceal failure.
paradoxes.measurement: Track class-specific mentor-to-apprentice paths, their availability during unannounced tests and aggregate hours.
paradoxes.falsifier: Loss of the stipulated final necessary path changes no unannounced recovery outcome because a verified substitute remains or the class was not necessary.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same specialization and joint practice increase robust recovery when gains are distributed across necessary complementary classes.

paradoxes.working_name: More common repairs, less independent error vocabulary
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A successful repair commons can increase solved case counts while reducing the range of novel failures it can recognize.
derivation: Widely reused repairs attract credit and funding.
Reviewers adopt the same compressed frame.
Independent boundary expertise and vocabulary reproduction decline.
New failures outside the common frame appear as familiar cases, preserving high measured completion.
assumptions: Common patches and summaries are genuinely useful.
Recognition of new classes requires independent conceptual work.
Funding and credit follow visible uptake rather than independent repertoire coverage.
paradoxes.counterexample: Commons credit supporting independently elicited boundary repertoires preserves or increases novel-class detection.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure solved incidents separately from blind new-class detection and independently elicited explanatory repertoire diversity.
paradoxes.falsifier: Greater shared repair adoption does not reduce independent vocabulary or blind novel-class recognition under the alleged budget displacement.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same shared repair commons can spread distinctions once found; maintaining independent discoverers lets common reuse amplify rather than suppress detection.

paradoxes.working_name: Every timing preference honored, nobody jointly participates
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Individually faithful scheduling and inherited commitments can leave no event satisfying the group's own shared-act criterion.
derivation: Private timing optimization scatters attendance.
Low quorum limits novice collective practice.
Inherited reconciliation consumes the current agenda.
Less collective organizing and renegotiation capacity sustains private scheduling dependence.
assumptions: A shared act requires a quorum in one interval.
Practice and agenda time reproduce the ability to renegotiate inherited constraints.
paradoxes.counterexample: Preferences having a common quorum interval, or protected joint rehearsal and present-agenda time, permit both individual respect and shared participation.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure individual timing satisfaction, actual simultaneous quorum, novice collective-role competence and current renegotiation agenda time.
paradoxes.falsifier: Private timing optimization raises shared quorum and preserves collective competence despite the stipulated incompatibility and agenda scarcity.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same faithful timing and inheritance can stabilize shared events when constraints overlap and negotiation maintains rather than consumes organizing capacity.

paradoxes.working_name: Same number of copies, more unrepresented claims
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A fixed-count lineage can require more representative assessment than before, so population-based capacity planning understates exclusion.
derivation: Branch count remains constant while relevant histories diverge.
The policy recognizes additional distinct claim classes.
Representation work competes with other legitimate constituencies.
Capacity pressure compresses conflicting claims, reducing timely stipulated coverage.
assumptions: No assumption of machine moral status is made; an institution stipulates a precautionary claim policy.
Shared review capacity is fixed and timely coverage requires some independent work for distinct claims.
paradoxes.counterexample: Histories diverge only in policy-irrelevant features, or additional independent assessment capacity is supplied.
paradoxes.measurement: At fixed copy count, measure relevant claim divergence, required independent reviewer time and omitted or delayed stipulated claims.
paradoxes.falsifier: Equal-count lineages with independently validated different claim distinctions require equal work and achieve equal timely coverage under the stated policy.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same divergence-aware policy supplies better representation when capacity responds to claim distinctions instead of raw copy count.

paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Narrower individual permissions can leave workers more dependent on an agent-mediated chain if institutions require that chain to perform the job.
derivation: Fragmentation increases reconstruction and intermediary needs.
Successful mediated execution becomes the occupational standard.
Declining any link risks failure to satisfy the standard.
More workers adopt the chain, reducing investment in independent recognized work routes.
assumptions: Caps genuinely reduce each local actor's permitted scope.
External execution and workplace recognition make the chain the accepted work route.
paradoxes.counterexample: Caps preserving a genuinely substitutable recognized manual route reduce local scope without creating occupational compulsion.
paradoxes.measurement: Compare largest local scope, required authorization-chain size, substitute recognized work routes and employment consequences of refusal.
paradoxes.falsifier: Tighter caps reduce chain size or preserve equal recognized non-chain performance when complementary task dependencies are present.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same narrowly scoped coordination improves safe occupational access when many interoperable alternatives can perform each necessary link.

scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Unsettled mandate-hours, arrival burst covariance and jointly available qualified disposition capacity.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: An initially finite synchronized stopping burst can become self-sustaining if delayed release creates additional reconciliation arrivals faster than dispositions remove them. The relevant boundary is state-dependent arrival work versus disposition capacity, not adoption percentage.
assumptions: Several mandates share restoration and assessment pools.
Waiting counterparties can create additional genuine reconciliation work.
At large institutional scope, shared settlement links must be demonstrated rather than assumed.

stages.conditional_prediction: One stop is normally settled if its work fits available reserve; the formal stop and recognized release may still differ.
stages.measurement: Record local stop time, residual obligations and disposition-hours.

stages.conditional_prediction: A common disturbance can synchronize 100 claims even if average daily workload is low; queue tail rises when their shared work exhausts burst reserve.
stages.measurement: Compare independent versus common-mode stop notifications, holding total claim work fixed.

stages.conditional_prediction: If adopters cluster on one settlement pool, this probe can cross saturation earlier than a uniformly dispersed 50% probe; no particular fraction is critical.
stages.measurement: Measure pool-specific simultaneous work and the additional reliance-generated arrival rate.

stages.conditional_prediction: If use-based funding has reduced reserve, a shared wave can enter a persistent arrears regime; equal nominal staffing need not imply equal unreserved capacity.
stages.measurement: Measure precommitted staffing separately from genuinely available disposition capacity.

stages.conditional_prediction: If independent substitute channels have disappeared, stopping can still be immediate locally while common recognized release remains slow; independently funded substitutes would avoid this.
stages.measurement: Measure substitute-path availability and recognized-release tail latency.

stages.conditional_prediction: A common clearing or recognition institution can couple otherwise competing providers' stop waves; independent clearing pools can uncouple them.
stages.measurement: Trace cross-provider residual obligations entering the same queue.

stages.conditional_prediction: Publicly mandated settlement deadlines can create a second synchronized peak or fund a protective disposition reserve, depending on policy.
stages.measurement: Compare calendar clustering and legally funded reserve rather than inferring an effect of regulation alone.

stages.conditional_prediction: Cross-jurisdiction recognition of unsettled mandates can propagate workload only along actual shared obligations; fragmented systems may instead bound the cascade.
stages.measurement: Measure the connected residual-obligation graph and work crossing jurisdictional interfaces.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same pooled settlement concentrates expertise and quickly clears synchronized stops when reserve scales with burst work and waiting does not generate uncontrolled new claims.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Same stop count, local permissions, total original work and staffing, but independent arrival schedules and a separate bounded residual-reliance queue.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: At verified shared capacity and endogenous reconciliation, increased arrival synchronization produces no persistent arrears or tail-release difference.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: Additional work may be bounded, clearing may automate safely, counterparties may waive reliance; no queue law or inevitable global cascade is asserted.

scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Independent counterparty recognition path count, smallest recognition cut and certifier share, measured separately from provider share.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Format proliferation draws on fixed adapter resources. A common certifier lowers local costs; adoption reduces maintenance of alternative paths. The discontinuity occurs when loss of the final independent proof path makes the certifier a necessary cut.
assumptions: Attestation formats are not automatically interoperable.
Counterparties maintain proof paths at positive cost.
Common certification can displace rather than merely supplement alternate maintenance.

stages.conditional_prediction: A single provider-to-counterparty proof path can be checked directly; certification need not be necessary.
stages.measurement: Observe actual accepted proofs and maintenance cost.

stages.conditional_prediction: One hundred providers may create many compatibility demands, but a common open proof format can keep adapter work low.
stages.measurement: Count distinct required transformations, not provider logos.

stages.conditional_prediction: An adopter cluster may choose a common certifier to conserve interpretation work; gate dependence remains contingent on alternative proof maintenance.
stages.measurement: Measure alternative proof acceptance before and after common certification.

stages.conditional_prediction: If resources follow certified transaction volume, alternate maintenance can fall below viability even while provider competition increases.
stages.measurement: Measure adapter funding, accepted alternate paths and provider versus certifier concentration.

stages.conditional_prediction: Loss of the last non-certifier path makes the gate necessary under the stipulated counterparty rule; 90% alone does not establish that loss.
stages.measurement: Attempt a valid transfer with the certifier unavailable.

stages.conditional_prediction: Entrants can competitively price service while all require the same recognition gate, shifting the bottleneck from service provision to standing.
stages.measurement: Compare provider switching with gate switching under fixed guarantees.

stages.conditional_prediction: Procurement or official acceptance can make one certification sufficient, exclusive, or merely optional; only exclusivity or path displacement creates the proposed cut.
stages.measurement: Inspect accepted proof alternatives and funded interoperability routes.

stages.conditional_prediction: Cross-border mutual recognition can either diversify proofs or align institutions on one inherited gate; the last-path test remains decisive.
stages.measurement: Construct the actual transnational proof graph and identify independent accepted routes.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same common certification reduces repeated interpretation and enables useful provider entry when multiple independent accepted proof routes remain viable.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Hold provider count, service quality and transaction volume fixed; vary whether independent adapters receive protected maintenance resources.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: More incompatible provider entry under verified fixed adapter capacity leaves alternate recognition paths intact and certifier dependence unchanged.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: The bottleneck may be a generic standard or ordinary network effect; this exercise asserts only the conditional measurement distinction, not new theoretical priority.

scale_transitions.working_name: Individual skills to extinct recovery complements
scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Number of required recovery classes with an independently available mentor-complement path at the moment of an unannounced shock.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Recovery is a complementary production hypergraph, not the sum of individual skill scores. A last essential class or mentor path can disappear while common-class practice grows. Success-conditioned reduction in mentoring makes the loss persist after hardware or route restoration.
assumptions: Some recovery tasks require multiple distinct skills.
Temporary announced-test help does not guarantee shock-time availability.
Mentor succession requires real class-specific practice.
Large-scale specialization or sharing may preserve complements and must be tested.

stages.conditional_prediction: One person can be individually competent but require an absent complementary helper; self-contained tasks avoid this condition.
stages.measurement: Map required skill combinations for one concrete recovery task.

stages.conditional_prediction: A network of 100 people can borrow rare skills for announced tests, masking local inability during an unannounced disturbance.
stages.measurement: Compare announced borrowing against simultaneous independent local availability.

stages.conditional_prediction: Adoption clustered around one specialist can remove enough ordinary encounters to interrupt succession locally, regardless of total adoption.
stages.measurement: Measure specialist mentoring contacts and local novice progress.

stages.conditional_prediction: Shared rare-class mentors may serve many apparently resilient sites; simultaneous failure can reveal that their advertised coverage was multiply counted.
stages.measurement: Conduct a bounded joint drill with total expert availability held fixed.

stages.conditional_prediction: If the last live mentor path retires, restoring average hours cannot immediately restore the missing complement; retained substitutes prevent the discontinuity.
stages.measurement: Track last-path loss and time to competent successor, not adoption rate itself.

stages.conditional_prediction: Provider-funded drills may assemble mobile expert help whose repeated success lowers each customer's local training budget.
stages.measurement: Record announced support transfers and local successor investment.

stages.conditional_prediction: Certification of aggregate hours can miss class extinction; class-specific apprentice-path requirements can preserve recovery diversity.
stages.measurement: Compare qualification coverage with actual simultaneous complementary performance.

stages.conditional_prediction: International specialization can preserve rare expertise cheaply or expose many sites to one unavailable complement; connectivity and shock independence determine which.
stages.measurement: Map real specialist pools, geographic covariance and transport or communication availability.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same sharing and joint demonstration teach local successors and maintain rare classes when they are used as apprenticeship rather than solely readiness evidence.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Match average skill, total training hours and equipment; protect one independent succession path for every required class.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Loss of an independently verified necessary class path creates no unannounced recovery deficit despite absence of a genuine substitute.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: The relevant complement may be unnecessary, substitutable or remotely available; evidence of an actual critical class is required before claiming any phase boundary.

scale_transitions.working_name: Courteous robot density to inherited access precedence
scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Recoverable manual-route capacity, persistent waiting footprint and the cost/time of reversing accommodation after mandates stop.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Each courteous interaction can be acceptable while aggregate waiting occupation creates temporary accommodation. Repeated accommodation becomes an inherited planning default; once independent route restoration costs exceed continuing accommodation, stopping individual robots no longer restores the earlier access regime.
assumptions: Waiting and yielding use physical space.
Repeated accommodations affect later design or access conventions.
Manual alternatives can decay or be removed.
Human users' observed movement is an incomplete measure of dormant needs.

stages.conditional_prediction: One yielding robot may improve access or impose negligible delay; a precedent need not form.
stages.measurement: Observe yielding, waiting footprint and displaced uses.

stages.conditional_prediction: Dense courteous waiting can exhaust a shared approach even with zero local etiquette violations.
stages.measurement: Measure concurrent stationary footprint and access, not collision count.

stages.conditional_prediction: A clustered installation can induce a temporary route concession before a uniformly dispersed higher-adoption setting.
stages.measurement: Compare equal robot counts with clustered and dispersed staging.

stages.conditional_prediction: Repeated concessions can become routine access expectations; maintenance decisions may stop protecting the old manual alternative.
stages.measurement: Record precedence changes, old-route maintenance and dormant users' claims.

stages.conditional_prediction: If restoring independent access exceeds the practical remedy horizon, stopping many robots leaves inherited redesign in place.
stages.measurement: Test physical route usability and restoration delay after simulated stop.

stages.conditional_prediction: Standard staging practices across suppliers can reproduce occupation even when customers switch providers.
stages.measurement: Measure supplier-independent waiting geometry and recognized access rules.

stages.conditional_prediction: Public access rules can preserve manual routes or ratify inherited accommodation; ordinary microgrants alone do not decide legitimacy.
stages.measurement: Measure protected independent access and the provenance of changed public defaults.

stages.conditional_prediction: Shared infrastructure standards can export staging conventions across cities, but local geometry and access law may prevent the same transition.
stages.measurement: Compare matched sites adopting the convention with independently protected routes.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same courteous repetition establishes reliable coordination and accessible shared spaces when staging and redesign preserve human alternatives and dormant needs.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Keep robot tasks, yielding compliance and movement volume fixed; constrain stationary staging footprints and preserve an independently usable route.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Repeated accommodation and documented manual-route decay do not increase reversal cost or persistent access precedence after stopping.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: Occupation need not harm anyone; redesign may genuinely improve access. The claimed variable is reversibility of alternatives, not a presumption against robots.

scale_transitions.working_name: Proposal output to institutional action reach
scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: External consequence reach of an unchanged proposal interface: resources, decisions or places reachable through accepted counterparty execution rules.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: External bridges turn proposals into transactions. Those executions create usage evidence that reallocates infrastructure, expanding what later proposals can execute. A change in institutional acceptance or infrastructure capacity—not a larger local permission set—can produce a discontinuous increase in reach.
assumptions: Some counterparties act on provisional outputs.
Added infrastructure actually extends executable outcomes.
All larger-scale institutional links are prospective models, not assertions of actual authority.

stages.conditional_prediction: One proposal can become an action when one counterparty has an execution bridge; without a bridge it remains advice.
stages.measurement: Trace a proposal to a verified external state change.

stages.conditional_prediction: Repeated execution may produce a stable demand signal while local proposal permissions remain fixed.
stages.measurement: Compare accepted proposal outputs and external transactions under the same interface.

stages.conditional_prediction: If accepted outputs are concentrated on one route or service, planners may cross an allocation threshold at this probe or another level.
stages.measurement: Identify the actual planning decision rule and its observed input.

stages.conditional_prediction: Allocation toward adapted use can increase executable reach and make independent channels less convenient, feeding further execution.
stages.measurement: Measure before/after physical capacity and availability of non-bridge routes.

stages.conditional_prediction: If external institutions now treat the output as routine, the same local proposal can affect a wider set of consequences than at entry; this is not automatically illegitimate.
stages.measurement: Hold local scope constant and measure the reachable external outcome set.

stages.conditional_prediction: Competing providers may share external execution institutions, so local switching changes authorship but not the expanded action channel.
stages.measurement: Compare provider-specific scope with common counterparty execution defaults.

stages.conditional_prediction: Official planning or acceptance can enlarge or limit proposal consequence reach; provenance of the public decision distinguishes authorized collective adaptation from drift.
stages.measurement: Record allocation decisions, accountability and explicit public authorization separately.

stages.conditional_prediction: Interoperable execution bridges can extend reach across jurisdictions, but absent acceptance or physical capacity breaks propagation.
stages.measurement: Test accepted cross-border transformations and the external resources actually reachable.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same execution-and-planning feedback builds useful infrastructure where accepted proposals reveal legitimate unmet needs and public allocation preserves meaningful independent channels.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Hold proposal outputs and local permission sets fixed; compare external execution without usage-responsive infrastructure allocation against the coupled condition.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Verified bridge execution and responsive planning change no external reachable outcomes under the fixed local interface.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: Allocation may reflect prior demand rather than agent-induced demand; macro reach is not necessarily coercive, harmful, unauthorized or commercially malicious.
